grh_a970470324e73e685055.title: DOA
paragraphs: Accountant and notary Frank Bigelow walks into a police station to report a murder, his own. While on a trip to San Francisco, someone slipped a lethal luminous poison into his drink, leaving him only days to live. Frank spends those final hours tracing the reason for his murder to a notarized bill of sale involving stolen iridium, a dead man named George Reynolds, and businessman Eugene Phillips. Each clue leads deeper into blackmail, murder, and an effort to silence anyone connected with the document. Frank finally identifies Halliday as the man who poisoned him at the Fisherman club and kills his own murderer in a final confrontation. After completing his statement to the police, Frank collapses and dies; the official report is marked with the grim abbreviation D.O.A., dead on arrival.

grh_a9b12ca5030dc16179ed.title: The Eyes of Mr. Leyton
paragraphs: American businessman Wayne Layton and his English rival Cholmondeley both approach Holmes over control of a valuable San Pedro concession, each fearing the other will use violence. Layton is later found fatally stabbed after entering a Limehouse hideout, and his dying attempt to name his killer sounds like 'Mandalay.' grh_a9712dbfffc6dd2932b0.title: Dog Story
paragraphs: Ten-year-old Tip finds a stray dog he names Jeff while his parents, Eleanor and Dick, are drifting toward a marital breakup. Eleanor believes Dick is involved with another woman, while Dick admits he has become infatuated and says the marriage is finished. Before the separation can harden, Tip falls through the ice on a pond and survives while Jeff dies in the same crisis. Their sons near loss and the dogs death force Dick and Eleanor to recognize how much they have taken for granted; they reconcile, later take Tip on a second honeymoon trip, and help him begin healing with a new puppy without pretending Jeff can be replaced.
